figures.finding: A resident pays 15% on the tax base up to 36 times the average wage (CZK 1,762,812 for 2026) and 23% above, less a basic credit of CZK 30,840 a year; there is no regional or municipal income tax.

sources.said: § 16 Sazba a výpočet daně pro základ daně (1) Sazba daně činí a) 15 % pro část základu daně do 36násobku průměrné mzdy a b) 23 % pro část základu daně přesahující 36násobek průměrné mzdy.

§ 35ba Slevy na dani pro poplatníky daně z příjmů fyzických osob (1) Poplatníkům uvedeným v § 2 se daň vypočtená podle § 16, případně snížená podle § 35, 35a nebo § 35b za zdaňovací období snižuje o a) základní slevu ve výši 30 840 Kč na poplatníka,
The 23% tax rate is applicable to income exceeding 36 times the average wage for the calendar year (CZK 1,762,812 for 2026).

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; a return, where required, is due by 1 April 2027 (1 May if filed electronically, 1 July through a tax adviser).

sources.said: Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year.

Where a tax return is required, it generally must be filed and any tax liability must be paid by 1 April of the following year. The deadline is 1 May of the following year if a tax return that is not filed by 1 April is subsequently filed electronically by the taxpayer, or 1 July of the following year if a tax return that is not filed by 1 April is subsequently filed by a tax advisor.

figures.finding: Tax on employment income is withheld by the employer and remitted to the tax authority; the self-employed file a return or may opt for the lump-sum regime.

sources.said: Tax on employment income is withheld by the employer and remitted to the tax authorities. Self- employed individuals (entrepreneurs) generally must file a tax return but have the option to be subject to a lump-sum tax

figures.finding: On gross pay the employer pays 24.8% social security and 9% health; the employee 11.6% (6.5% pension, 0.6% sickness, 4.5% health). A self-employed person pays 42.7% (28% pension, 1.2% unemployment, 13.5% health) on an assessment base of at least 55% of the income tax base. Social security stops at 48 times the average wage (CZK 2,350,416 for 2026); health has no ceiling.

selfEmployed.base: at least 55% of the income tax base

sources.said: An employer contributes 9% of the employee’s gross salary to the state health insurance funds and 24.8% of the employee’s gross salary to the state social security funds. An employee contributes 11.6% of gross income (4.5% health insurance, 6.5% old-age pension, 0.6% sickness insurance). A self-employed individual is subject to a mandatory contribution of 42.7% (13.5% health insurance, 28% old-age pension, 1.2% unemployment) on the assessment base (determined as at least 55% of the income tax base).

There is no maximum assessment base for health insurance purposes. The maximum assessment base for social security purposes (i.e., old-age pension contributions and unemployment insurance, applicable in the case of both the employee and the employer, as well as for a self-employed individual) is 48 times the average wage for the calendar year (CZK 2,350,416 for 2026).

figures.finding: A non-resident performer's fee for an appearance in the Czech Republic, whoever receives it, is Czech-source income taxed by a 15% special rate withheld at source (35% for residents of non-EU/EEA states without a treaty or information-exchange agreement).

value.base: gross income from personal public performance in the Czech Republic

A 35% rate applies where dividends are paid to a resident of a non- EU or non-EEA jurisdiction with which the Czech Republic does not have a tax treaty or a tax information exchange agreement (TIEA).

figures.finding: A freelancer must register for VAT once supplies in the Czech Republic exceed CZK 2 million in a calendar year (payer from 1 January following), or at once on passing CZK 2,536,500; the standard rate is 21%, reduced 12%.
figures.applies: Persons making supplies in the Czech Republic (the source states it for companies; the same thresholds are in the VAT Act for any person).

sources.said: The standard VAT rate is 21%. A reduced rate of 12% applies to certain supplies

A Czech company must register for VAT if its supplies in the Czech Republic exceed CZK 2 million in a calendar year. In this case, the Czech company will become a VAT payer starting from 1 January of the following year. However, if a Czech company’s supplies in the Czech Republic exceed CZK 2,536,500 in a calendar year, the company will become a VAT payer on the date immediately following the date this threshold is exceeded.

figures.finding: An author's fee for a contribution to a newspaper, magazine, radio or television from Czech sources, up to CZK 10,000 a month from one payer, is a separate base taxed by withholding at the special rate (15%); other self-employed income, an author's included, may deduct flat expenses of 40% (capped at CZK 800,000).
